events.text: Elder Dang Moryeon finds you at the charcoal burners' camp and warms his hands at a fire that is not giving any heat. "You keep your dead on a rope like a farmer keeps ducks," he says. "They are owed something, you know. So are you. There is a thing the Court does with a grudge that has nowhere to go. We send it somewhere."

choices.text: Ask him what it costs

effects.log: He tells you, and he does not soften any of it. By the time the fire has gone out, you know how to give a wonhon a name to walk towards.

choices.text: Say you will think about it

effects.log: He nods as if you had agreed. "The grudges will wait," he says. "They are good at that." If you want it, the Court knows where you are.

events.text: He takes you to a boundary stone at the edge of a burned village, and has you hold the cord while he talks. A curse, says Elder Dang Moryeon, is only a grudge with directions. Give the wonhon a name. Give it a door, a gate, a road home. Then let go, and do not watch it leave, because some of them look back.

choices.text: Practise on the cord until your hands stop shaking

effects.log: Your hands stop shaking on the third night, which is not as comforting as you had expected. You have The Sent Grudge.

choices.text: Ask what became of the last student

effects.log: "That one looked back," he says, and he hands you the cord again. You have The Sent Grudge, and a habit of walking away without turning your head.

events.text: The old knots are what the shrine's rites untie, says Elder Dang Moryeon, knot by knot on the white cloth, until the dead can go. The Court only learned to do it backwards. He ties one around your wrist so that you feel it, and he makes you swear to pass him the salt. When you reach for the wine instead, the whole arm goes dead to the shoulder. He passes you the salt.

choices.text: Learn to tie it

effects.log: You learn it, and you learn where in a life to tie it: on an oath never to raise a hand, or on a limit never to be passed. Betray it and it draws tight. You have the Knot-Oath.

choices.text: Learn how it is cut, too

effects.log: He laughs for the first time you have ever seen. "Everyone who ties one should know," he says, and he shows you. You have the Knot-Oath, and you sleep a little worse for knowing how little it takes.

events.text: It takes the Court a year to arrange, and it happens in a salt store with no windows. Mo Sangwol, the Name-Eater, looks like somebody's kindly uncle. He asks what you are called, and then he asks again, and the second time it takes you a moment. "There," he says. "Everything is held up by what it is called. You only have to pull on the right thread."

choices.text: Learn it from him

effects.log: He teaches well, and he is patient, and he thanks you for coming. You walk home saying the names of everyone you know, out loud, all the way. You have the Name-Erasing Curse.

choices.text: Keep your own name folded in your sleeve while he teaches

effects.log: You write it on a slip and you keep it in your sleeve for the whole lesson. He sees, and it delights him. You have the Name-Erasing Curse, and you keep the slip.

events.text: It takes the Court a year to arrange, and it happens in a salt store with no windows. Your soul knows this work. You know what the mornings are like, and how a face goes on looking at you while you search for what comes next. Mo Sangwol sees that at once. "Oh, you have been on the other end," he says warmly. "Then this will not take long at all."

choices.text: Learn it, knowing exactly what it is

effects.log: It does not take long. You have never been so quick at anything. You have the Name-Erasing Curse, and the heart demon has been listening.

choices.text: Learn it, and tell him you will come for him afterwards

effects.log: He writes that down, pleased, in a little book of promises. You have the Name-Erasing Curse. The book, you notice, is nearly full.

events.text: A coffin-maker's boy brings you a slip of grave-cloth with an elder's name on it, a sect's mark and nothing else. The Court does not say why. It rarely does. It pays in death qi, and it has a long memory for who said no.

choices.text: Send a wonhon after the name

effects.log: You take the strongest off your rope and give it the name. The boy waits to see it done, then runs off whistling.

choices.text: Send the slip back, unopened where it matters

effects.log: You send it back with the boy. Elder Dang Moryeon does not reply, and his silence is not much warmer than his company.

events.text: Elder Dang Moryeon sits down beside you at a funeral, which is where he prefers to do business. "An elder is going to rule on the matter of a certain graveyard," he says, looking straight ahead. "The Court would rather it were someone else. Nothing dramatic. A few bad years, and a retirement. You understand we would be grateful."

choices.text: Say you will see to it

effects.log: He pats your knee and offers his condolences to the widow, whom he has never met. By nightfall a wonhon is walking towards a sect it has never seen.

choices.text: Say the Court can do its own haunting

effects.log: "It generally does," he says, and he goes on sitting there until the end of the service, just to make sure you know he has plenty of time.

events.text: A jar arrives with no sender, sealed in grave-cloth, cold as a well in spring. That is the Court's payment, and the Court's way of saying the graveyard's business has been settled. Nobody has thanked you. They never will.

choices.text: Drink what is in it

effects.log: It runs down into you, and for an hour you cannot feel your hands. The Court has paid in full.

choices.text: Pour it on the rope instead

effects.log: The rope drinks it and hums for three nights. The Court has paid in full, and the dog next door has moved house.

events.text: You choose a crossroads, as you were taught, and tie the name on with a thread of your own hair. The wonhon that comes off the rope was {crt_who}, {crt_wrong}. It has never heard of {crt_name}. You tell it about {crt_name} anyway. After you have finished, it stands there a while, and then it goes where you pointed. It does not ask if this is right. That is rather the trouble with them.

choices.text: Walk away without looking back

effects.log: You walk away and you do not look back. Behind you, the crossroads gets colder, and then it gets warmer, which is worse.

choices.text: Say the whole name three times, so that it cannot lose its way

effects.log: You say it three times, and it is a good clear night for it. Somewhere, {crt_name} stops halfway through a sentence and forgets what the sentence was.

events.text: You have thought about {crt_name} for years, and it surprises you how little there is to say to the wonhon now. It was {crt_who}, {crt_wrong}. You could tell it what {crt_he} did to you, but it does not care about that. It only wants to know that someone, somewhere, is still warm. You show it which way.

choices.text: Tell it anyway

effects.log: You tell it everything: every slight, in order. It listens with its whole cold attention. You feel a good deal better, and that ought to worry you.

choices.text: Say nothing, and untie it

effects.log: You untie it and say nothing. There is a dignity in that, or at least there is a silence, and you stand in it until morning.

events.text: The ground has not thawed, and even so the wonhon leaves a track. It was {crt_who}, {crt_wrong}, and the {crt_grade} ones do not walk towards a name, they lean on the whole road until the road tips. You have sent it at {crt_name}, {crt_title}. All along the way, the dogs of three villages go under their porches and refuse to come out.

choices.text: Watch it to the edge of the valley

effects.log: You stand and watch it to the edge of the valley. You were told not to. It does not look back. Not this time.

choices.text: Go home quickly, and bar the door

effects.log: You bar the door, which is ridiculous, and sleep beside it. The rope is lighter by one. You had not known how much it weighed.

events.text: An elder is a hard thing to reach: wards at the gate, juniors on every stair, a century of good habits. But {crt_name}, {crt_title}, has a morning walk, and once, in that long life, {crt_he} must have stepped over someone. The wonhon was {crt_who}, {crt_wrong}. It only needs the one small door. You give it the walk.

choices.text: Give it the time of day as well

effects.log: You give it the hour and the stair. There is an art to this, and the wretched thing is that you are good at it.

choices.text: Burn the slip with the name on it

effects.log: You burn the slip and you bury the ash at the crossroads. Now it is just you and the wonhon who know. And Elder Dang Moryeon, naturally.

events.text: They sing about {crt_name} in the wine shops: {crt_title}. You have heard the song. So you sing it to the wonhon, all of it, on a hill at night. It was {crt_who}, {crt_wrong}, and nobody ever made a song for it. You can feel it paying attention. It is the first time the rope has ever gone quiet at the same moment as you.

choices.text: Sing the last verse twice

effects.log: You sing the last verse twice, and the second time your voice does not sound like yours. It goes. The hill is yours, for what it is worth.

choices.text: Leave off before the end

effects.log: You leave off before the end. Let it hear the rest from the living. It goes, in the direction of the applause.

events.text: It is not done at a crossroads. It is done at a naming stone, where parents bring their newborns. You say {crt_name} to the wonhon, and then you say the names of {crt_his} people, every one you could buy, and at each name the wonhon of {crt_who} takes a small breath, as if it had been given something to eat. When you have finished, you find you are whispering them. You make yourself stop.

choices.text: Scrape the stone clean afterwards

effects.log: You scrape the moss off the place. Three families will bring their newborns here this spring. It is the least you can do, and you know exactly how little that is.

choices.text: Leave it as it is, and go

effects.log: You leave it. On the road home a child asks you the time of day, and calls you by the wrong name, and laughs. You do not laugh.

events.text: You know what you are sending. You know the morning it arrives: the face at the table, looking at you, kind and tired, and that small hole in the air where a word used to be. You knew it would be hard to do this. It turns out to be easy, and you would like someone to answer for that. {crt_name} will wake up soon. The wonhon of {crt_who} goes off with its mouth full.

choices.text: Say the name of someone you love, out loud

effects.log: You say it. It is still there. You say it again. You go on saying it for some time, and the rope hums along.

choices.text: Sit down at the stone until it is light

effects.log: You sit until it is light. Nobody comes, and nobody ever comes. The heart demon sits with you, and it is good company, considering.

events.text: Your news of {crt_name} comes secondhand, as it should. {crt_His} well has gone bitter, and {crt_his} horse will not pass the gate. {crt_He} has had the same dream three nights, a person standing in a doorway with water running off them. {crt_He} laughs about it in the tea house, but everyone there has noticed {crt_he} now sits facing the door.

choices.text: Send a little of yourself after it

effects.log: You breathe on the rope at dusk, and it twitches like a dog dreaming. The next letter says that the well has gone black.

choices.text: Go and take tea in that same tea house, and watch

effects.log: You take a table by the window. {crt_name} looks straight at you, and {crt_he} has no idea. It is the best tea you have ever had, and you do not sleep afterwards.

events.text: The juniors of {crt_name} have started to whisper. There was a nosebleed in the middle of a lecture. The incense in {crt_his} room burns down in a single hour. {crt_He} has sent to the sect's physician, who can find nothing, and to the sect's library, which has been very quiet about what it found. An elder does not say that {crt_he} is afraid. {crt_He} merely walks a different way to morning practice.

choices.text: Learn the new way

effects.log: You pay a kitchen boy two coppers, and you tell the wonhon about the new way. It takes this rather well.

choices.text: Leave it be, and let it work

effects.log: You leave it be. A season passes, and {crt_name} changes the way again. Nobody can walk away from a thing like this for long.

events.text: {crt_title}: {crt_name} has dropped a sword. It happened in front of a whole courtyard of young people who had come a long way to watch {crt_him} do something with it. {crt_He} made a joke, and they laughed as they were meant to, and picked it up for {crt_him}. The rankings have not moved. But in the wine shops someone has already started to change a verse.

choices.text: Buy a round in that wine shop

effects.log: You buy a round, and you ask to hear the new verse, and you have the singer do it twice. It is a small pleasure. It costs you more than the wine.

choices.text: Stay away from it, and stay quiet

effects.log: You stay away. There is no rule that says you must watch. You find you know how it is going in any case; you only have to look at the rope.

events.text: {crt_name} has lost a whole rung between one harvest and the next, the way a house loses its heat. The neighbours have stopped calling. {crt_His} {crt_rel}, {crt_kin}, goes from physician to physician with {crt_his} wrists written out on a sheet of paper. You saw the sheet. Someone asked whether you could help, as a mudang. You looked at it for some time.

choices.text: Say that you cannot help, and hand it back

effects.log: You hand it back. {crt_kin} thanks you, and bows, and goes off down the road to the next one. You stand there until the sound of it has gone.

choices.text: Keep the sheet, for the rope to read

effects.log: You say you will look into it, and you keep the sheet. It takes the rope a week to get through it, and then {crt_name} loses the use of the left hand.

events.text: They have carried {crt_name} down from morning practice, a rung less than {crt_he} was. The sect gives out that {crt_he} is in closed-door seclusion. {crt_kin}, {crt_his} {crt_rel}, sits outside the door all the same, reading the sutras in a steady voice, and nobody can make {crt_khim} go to bed. The other elders have begun, very politely, to discuss who will take the lectures.

choices.text: Pour your death qi after it

effects.log: The door gets colder, and the reading goes on. You find it is hard to listen to, from this far off, and you can hear it all the same.

choices.text: Hold it where it is

effects.log: You hold it just there, and you do not press. The reading goes on. It is a strange thing, to be so careful with someone you are destroying.

events.text: {crt_title}, {crt_name} has lost a rung. {crt_He} was challenged on a bridge by somebody nobody had ever heard of, and {crt_he} lost, and {crt_he} looked more surprised than hurt. {crt_kin}, {crt_his} {crt_rel}, helped {crt_him} back through a crowd that was already adjusting its opinions. Young people who had crossed provinces to bow have started finding that they had other business in the area.

choices.text: Go and see the bridge

effects.log: You go. There is nothing to see but a river and a good view. You stand on it for a while, feeling very large and rather sick.

choices.text: Feed it, while the crowd is turning

effects.log: It knows where to go now, and you only have to send it the means. By the first frost, {crt_name} cannot lift {crt_his} own sword.

events.text: {crt_name} has climbed to the Salt Road hermitage, and Abbot Cheonggong has looked at the shadow {crt_he} casts, and has sent everyone else out. For forty-nine days now there have been monks chanting in shifts. You can feel it from here, a steady pressure on the rope, like a thumb on a bruise. The abbot is not angry. You can tell that from the chanting. He is only very, very thorough.

choices.text: Pour death qi after it, and pull

effects.log: You wrap the rope around your arm and you pull. Whatever comes of it, it will come of that.

choices.text: Hold still, and let it hold or not

effects.log: You hold still, and you listen to the rope. Nobody ever told you that this would be the hard part.

choices.text: Call it back while you still can

effects.log: You take hold of the rope, and you begin to call. You had not thought you would.

events.text: You feel it the moment she starts: a hand on the rope that knows the rope. {crt_name} has gone to Mudang Seori, who sat beside you at Spirit-Mother Bongnye's knee and learned the same songs. She has sung the wonhon's name by its true grudge, {crt_who}, {crt_wrong}, and she has asked it, very gently, why it is doing this for you. It is listening to her. You had forgotten how well she sings.

events.text: Peach-wood stakes have gone in around the house of {crt_name}, and every doorpost has a Wudang talisman on it, written in a hand you have started to recognise. This is what Yun Haksan does when he cannot find the sorcerer yet: he makes the sorcerer's work very expensive. Somewhere in the walls of that house, the wonhon of {crt_who} is trying each door in turn.

events.text: {crt_name} has stopped asking for help. {crt_He} has sent everyone away and sits up alone at night with a lamp and a sword across {crt_his} knees, talking to the wonhon. Your spies say {crt_he} is apologising, in a general way, to anyone {crt_he} may have wronged. {crt_He} has a long list. It is the most dangerous thing {crt_he} could have done, and you doubt {crt_he} knows it. That kind of thing can loosen a knot.

events.text: It holds. The news reaches you by way of a tired physician: {crt_name} has been sent home, with kindly words and a recipe for broth. Everything that could be done has been done. The rope is quiet, and it lies in your hand as calm as an old dog that has just come back from somewhere you will not ask about.

choices.text: Coil it up and go to bed

effects.log: You sleep well. You would very much like not to have slept so well.

choices.text: Make an offering at the crossroads

effects.log: You leave rice and a little wine at the crossroads. You are not sure who you are thanking, and you take care not to find out.

events.text: {crt_kin}, {crt_rel} of {crt_name}, has found out who you are. It took {crt_khim} four years and most of what the house had left. {crt_kHe} does not come with a sword. {crt_kHe} comes on foot, in the rain, and kneels on your step with a box of silver, and says quite plainly that {crt_khe} knows what you are and what you have done, and asks you what it would take.

choices.text: Take the silver, and call it back

effects.log: {crt_kin} does not thank you. {crt_kHe} merely breathes out, as though for the first time in four years.

choices.text: Call it back, and leave the box where it is

effects.log: You call it back, and you push the box across the step with your foot. {crt_kin} stares at you. {crt_kHe} has no idea what to do with this, and neither do you.

choices.text: Shut the door

effects.log: You shut the door. {crt_kin} stays on the step until morning. Then the step is empty, and you know that {crt_khe} will not be kneeling the next time.

events.text: There is someone at the shrine asking for you by the wrong name, and that is how you know the matter has got close. {crt_kin} has brought {crt_name} along, in a cart. {crt_kHe} wants you to look. {crt_kHe} does not say a word, {crt_khe} merely turns back the blanket, and {crt_name} looks up at you, thinner than you thought anyone could be, and asks politely if you are the physician.

choices.text: Say that you are, and call it back while you hold {crt_his} wrist

effects.log: You hold the wrist, and you call it back, and you prescribe broth. {crt_kin} watches every move your hands make, and {crt_khe} will remember them.

choices.text: Take the fee, and call it back

effects.log: You name a fee. {crt_kin} pays it without a word, and that is how you find out what a person can look like when they are not saying anything.

choices.text: Say there is nothing to be done

effects.log: You say it in a physician's voice. It is a very good one. The cart goes away down the hill, and you stand there until it is out of sight, and for a while afterwards.

events.text: {crt_name} has not got up since the first hard frost. Three people still visit. {crt_He} has stopped asking what is wrong. The other evening, they say, {crt_he} asked after you, of all people; {crt_he} has been going through the years. You have only to close your hand. The wonhon of {crt_who} sits at the foot of the bed, looking back at you, waiting.

choices.text: Let it finish

effects.log: You open your hand on the rope. There is no noise at all.

choices.text: Stop here, and leave {crt_him} alive with what is left

effects.log: You stop here. It is not mercy, and nobody will mistake it for that. It may be something worse.

choices.text: Offer it: swear the oath, and live

effects.log: You send {crt_him} the words, by way of the wonhon. {crt_name} has been waiting a long time for someone to offer {crt_him} anything.

choices.text: Call it back, even now

effects.log: You call it back. It comes slowly, and it resents you, and you can feel exactly what it has been eating.

events.text: They carry {crt_name} out to the sun in the afternoons now. {crt_He} cannot always say which disciple is which. The sect has a new elder, who was very gracious about it. {crt_kin} still reads to {crt_him}. At the foot of the chair, where no one looks, the wonhon of {crt_who} stands on the warm flagstones, leaving a damp mark. It would like to know what next.

At the turn of the stair, the wonhon sits waiting for your word.

events.text: They bury {crt_name} on a clear morning. You go; a mudang has every reason to. Nobody at the graveside knows yet. You perform the rites, since nobody asked anyone else, and you are very good. {crt_kin} bows to you afterwards and thanks you for your trouble. The wonhon of {crt_who} is gone, it had nothing left to stay for, and you can feel the place on the rope where it used to be.

choices.text: Take the fee

effects.log: You take the fee. You could hardly refuse: it would have looked strange. It is the heaviest handful of coins you have ever carried.

choices.text: Stay behind, and tidy the grave

effects.log: You stay behind until they have gone, and you straighten the offerings, and you pull up a weed. Nobody sees. There is nobody it would help.

events.text: {crt_name} is dead of nothing. That is what the physicians say, and {crt_title} or not, that is what they will carve. You had thought about this day often, in the early years, and in your thoughts you were always there. As it happens, you are at the market, buying radishes, when the rope goes slack in your sleeve. The radish seller asks you if you are feeling quite well. You tell her that you are, and you pay her.

choices.text: Go home, and make soup

effects.log: You make soup. It is a good soup. You eat it. There does not seem to be anything else that happens next.

choices.text: Tell someone. Anyone

effects.log: You tell the radish seller. She laughs, and says you should get more sleep. You agree with her, and you go on standing there, holding the radishes.

events.text: You stop it there. {crt_name} wakes up one morning with the cold gone out of the room, and {crt_he} lies there a long time before {crt_he} dares to breathe in. {crt_He} is alive, with a third of what {crt_he} was. {crt_He} will try to climb back. They always try. What {crt_he} will not do again is sleep with {crt_his} back to a door. The wonhon of {crt_who} has gone home, having eaten.

choices.text: Send a small gift, with no name on it

effects.log: You send a jar of good honey, for the throat, with no name on it. It is the cruellest thing you have ever done, and you are not certain why you did it.

choices.text: Put it out of your mind

effects.log: You put it out of your mind, and it stays out, for hours at a time. That is what the Court calls a clean finish.

events.text: You stop it there. {crt_name} has given up the lectures, and it was announced with great respect. Now and then {crt_he} is wheeled out to be shown to visitors. {crt_kin} has been told that, with care, {crt_he} may see ten more years. That young person has sat down on the step and for the first time in all this has begun to think, carefully and with a clear head, about who could have done it.

choices.text: Light a stick of incense for the old elder

effects.log: You light it at the shrine, in the ordinary way, along with all the others. The smoke goes straight up. It tells you nothing at all.

choices.text: Find out what {crt_kin} has been reading

effects.log: You pay a copyist. {crt_kin} has been reading about the Unburied Court. You sit with that for a while, with your hand on the rope.

events.text: You stop it there. {crt_name} is alive, in a town where nobody much asks, teaching children their strokes. The song has a new last verse, kinder than you would have thought. Sometimes a traveller stops at the door and asks if {crt_he} is really the one. {crt_He} says no. You have got what you wanted, and it is teaching children in a dyer's town.

choices.text: Walk through that town once

Yun Haksan unties the cord from his sword. "I will not ask you again what you have been doing," he says. "I have read the walls of the houses. I am only going to cut what you have out, now, and you may try to stop me."

choices.text: Try to stop him

ok.log: You leave him on one knee in the mud, breathing hard, and he looks more interested than he has ever looked. "Well," he says. "Wudang will want to know about that." You go on, with your rope and your work, and your ribs ache.

fail.log: Peach wood turns out to be very hard. You are lying in the road with rain falling in your eyes, and he stands over you and does exactly what he said. It takes him no time at all.

choices.text: Hold out your rope, and renounce it all

effects.log: You hold it out, the whole length of it. He does not take it. "Untie the rest yourself," he says. "That is the part that counts."

choices.text: Get away over the river

ok.log: You go off the road and into the reeds, and you are on the far bank before he has finished tying up his sword. You leave the district that night. He will have to start all over again.

fail.log: You are halfway across when you hear his sword go by. It does not touch you. It does not need to; there is a talisman on your back now, and you do not find it for a week.

events.text: He has grown old on your account. You had not thought of it until you see him at the foot of the shrine stair, one hand on a stick, the peach-wood sword on his back grey with handling. He has come alone. "All Wudang thinks this is a waste of my last few years," says Yun Haksan. "They are quite right. Come down, please. My knees will not do those steps. Bring the rope. One of us will not need it after today."

choices.text: Come down, and finish it

ok.log: It takes until dusk. He sits down on the bottom step at last and lays the sword across his knees. "No," he says, to no one, and he takes a while to get his breath. "No, that is all I have." He goes home to the mountain. Nobody ever hunts you again, and you had not known that you would miss it.

fail.log: It takes until dusk. When it is over, you cannot feel your hands, and he is kneeling beside you, tying something around your wrists with great care. It is a straw rope, just like the one she used. "There," he says. "Now you may rest as well."

choices.text: Come down, and hand him the rites

effects.log: You come down. It is a long stair. You say what you have to say, all of it, and he listens, and at the end of it he nods as if you had told him the time. "Good," he says. "My knees thank you."

events.text: It is done, and it is done properly. There is nothing you could point to: your hands work, and the rope is only a rope, and the dead still come to you with their griefs. But when you reach for the old cold road that you used to send things down, there is a wall there now, with a Wudang talisman on it, written in a hand you know very well. The Court has struck your name. Elder Dang Moryeon sent back your cup.

choices.text: Go on being a mudang, since it seems you still are

effects.log: You ring your bell at the next door. An old woman wants to know if her husband is at peace. You find out. It is a living.

choices.text: Throw the cup in the river

effects.log: You throw it in the river. It does not sink at once. It floats for a while, in no particular hurry, as he would have done.

events.text: You walk up the hill with all of it: the cords, the slips, the little book of hours and stairways. Spirit-Mother Bongnye is at the top, cutting straw, the fires already lit. She takes it from you, piece by piece, and it takes a long time to burn. The straw rope is gone from the inner door. "The debts stay," she says. "Sit. You will want something to eat."

choices.text: Sit, and eat

effects.log: You sit and you eat. It is the same thin soup as ever. You had forgotten it. The Court sends you a coffin the next day, with your name crossed out, and you use it for firewood.

choices.text: Ask how long it takes

effects.log: You ask her how long it takes, to be clear of it. She laughs until she has to wipe her eyes. It is the first time you have ever seen that. She gives you more soup.

events.text: Somebody says the name of {crt_name} in the market, and you turn your head before you can think. You can no longer hear it without a slight pull at the wrist, the way a kite tugs when there is no wind down where you are. The rope would like you to know that it is thinking about that person all the time now, and that you are too.

choices.text: Think about something else

effects.log: You think about something else. It takes some effort, and then you are thinking about how much effort it took, and then you are back.

choices.text: Let yourself think about it

effects.log: You let yourself. It is quite restful, in its way. You lose most of an afternoon, and you could not say where it went.

events.text: It rained today and you found you had laid an extra place at the table. You do not remember doing it. There is a bowl and a spoon and a cup, and the cushion is a little damp. The wonhon of {crt_who} is a long way from here, about the business you gave it. Still, it seems to feel it has a home to come back to. Your neighbours have stopped dropping in. You cannot blame them.

choices.text: Clear the place away

effects.log: You clear it away, and you dry the cushion. Tomorrow, you will find out whether or not you are the one who does it.

choices.text: Leave it. It is a small thing to give

effects.log: You leave it there. It seems only polite. By the end of the month there is a little water standing in the bowl.

events.text: As a child you would not let anyone tie a thread around your wrist, not even for a birthday. Now you pass a shrine with its five-coloured cords in the wind, and a coldness goes through you from a life you never lived. Your fingers know a knot. They make it on your sleeve before you can stop them, three turns, perfectly. You stand there undoing it for a long time.

choices.text: Leave an offering, for whoever it was

effects.log: You leave a little rice at the shrine. It is for no one you can name. You have an odd sense of a very long debt, and of having made one small payment.

choices.text: Remember how the knot goes

effects.log: You remember how it goes. You could not say why you would want to. You remember anyway, the way you remember how to swim.

events.text: You wait for the new moon and go down to the old ferry steps. The wonhon of {crt_who} comes off the rope without a sound, and you whisper it everything it needs: a name, {crt_name}, and the way there. It was {crt_wrong}. It seems a long time since anyone told it where to go. The water goes flat as it passes.

choices.text: Rinse your hands in the river

effects.log: You rinse them. It does nothing, but the cold is honest, and you go home.

choices.text: Throw a coin in after it

effects.log: You throw in a coin, for the ferryman, in case there is one. It is the kind of thing a person does. You are still a person, you think.

events.text: A curse wants something of theirs, Elder Dang Moryeon says, and you have it: a thread from a sleeve, come by honestly enough. You wind it into the rope around the wonhon of {crt_who} and it goes still, like a hound given a glove. {crt_name} is in another province, sitting down to supper. There is no hurry at all.

choices.text: Burn what is left of the thread

effects.log: It goes up with a small smell of someone else. You open a window, and then you close it.

choices.text: Keep a little of it

effects.log: You keep an inch in a fold of paper. One never knows. You are beginning to sound like him.

events.text: An elder of {crt_name}'s years gives nobody an easy way in. But every sect keeps a wall of its dead, and {crt_his} teacher is on it, and {crt_he} still goes there at the turn of the year. You send the wonhon of {crt_who} to wait by that wall. It has no objection to waiting. It has been doing that since it was {crt_wrong}.

choices.text: Give it the date

effects.log: You give it the date. A person ought to be left alone at a teacher's grave, and that is exactly why it will work.

choices.text: Let it find the hour for itself

effects.log: You let it find the hour. It gives you the odd comfort of not having chosen.

events.text: It is hard to hate a stranger, and {crt_name}, {crt_title}, is only a stranger with a good title. So you buy the woodcut they sell at fairs, and you pin it up, and you look at it for a season until you have found something. The wonhon of {crt_who} does not need that much. You send it with the woodcut folded in its keeping.

choices.text: Take the woodcut down afterwards

effects.log: You take it down. There is a pale square on the wall, and you hang a calendar over it.

choices.text: Leave it up, and buy another

effects.log: You leave it up. The fair sells them by the dozen. Soon they will be worth something, or nothing.

events.text: No wonhon has ever walked into the hall of {crt_name}, {crt_title}: there are too many banners, too many sworn people, too many talismans over the door. But a banner has to be mended. You send the wonhon of {crt_who} in with the mending, stitched into a hem, on its way to the one person who sits beneath it all day.

choices.text: Pay the seamstress well

effects.log: You pay her well, and she will never know why. She buys her daughter new shoes with it.

choices.text: Pick the thread yourself, and say nothing

effects.log: You pick it yourself, a good dark red. Nobody looks closely at the back of a banner. That has always been true of everything.

events.text: A house that large is only a great many people who have agreed to obey {crt_name}, {crt_title}. You do not need to reach the head. You need the wonhon of {crt_who} to sit on the threshold, where they all step over, and let them begin to wonder. You lay a little grave-earth under the third step and walk off with your bell.

choices.text: Stay for the morning bell

effects.log: You stay, a nobody at the gate. Forty people go in over that step, and the last one stumbles. You leave.

choices.text: Be two provinces away by the morning

effects.log: You are two provinces away by the morning, with witnesses. Elder Dang Moryeon would approve. You try not to think of that.

events.text: It is a little thing, the first news of {crt_name}. {crt_His} ink will not dry. Every letter {crt_he} writes this month is smudged by morning, and {crt_he} has begun to blame the servants. A mudang would know that smell of river in the study. {crt_He} is not a person who has ever needed a mudang. Not yet.

choices.text: Wait

effects.log: You wait. It is what this work mostly is. Nobody ever tells the young that.

choices.text: Send a pedlar past, offering charms

effects.log: A pedlar goes by the gate with cheap charms. {crt_name} buys one, laughing, and that is how it starts.

events.text: Dogs have begun to dislike {crt_name}. It started with {crt_his} own, and now the ones in the street. A child at the well said there was somebody walking behind {crt_him}, all wet, and got a slap for it from a frightened mother. You hear it all from a salt carter who thinks it the funniest thing this side of the river.

choices.text: Laugh along with the carter

effects.log: You laugh in the right place. You are getting good at the right places.

choices.text: Ask after the child

effects.log: You ask. The child is well. It should not matter to you. You note that it does, and you go on with your day.

events.text: {crt_name} has moved {crt_his} bed. A rival of many years does not take notes on such a thing unless {crt_he} has a reason, you tell yourself, and you have been keeping notes. Then {crt_he} moved it back. Then {crt_he} had the floor taken up. The carpenter says there was nothing under it, and that {crt_he} tipped well and would not meet his eye.

choices.text: Hire that carpenter for something small

effects.log: You have him mend a shelf and you let him talk. It is a very well mended shelf.

choices.text: Stop keeping notes

effects.log: You burn the notes. You find you remember them all regardless.

events.text: The sect's morning bell cracked last week, and the disciples of {crt_name} say it cracked as {crt_he} passed. That is nonsense, of course. It is also now the only thing that anyone says. {crt_He} has given a very good lecture on superstition. They all took notes, and sat a little further from {crt_him} than they usually do.

choices.text: Get a copy of that lecture

effects.log: It really is good. You read it twice, and you agree with most of it. The rope does not.

choices.text: Let them talk

effects.log: You let them talk. A bell can be recast. The rest of it cannot.

events.text: In the hall of {crt_name}, {crt_title}, the great lamp will not stay lit on the seat side of the room. The stewards have changed the oil, then the wick, then the steward. Nobody mentions it where {crt_he} can hear. {crt_He} has started holding audience in the afternoons, for the light, and calls it a concession to the old.

choices.text: Learn who has noticed

effects.log: A cousin has noticed. There is always a cousin. You write the name down.

choices.text: Leave them to their lamps

effects.log: You leave them to it. A house can feel its own weather before anyone will say it is raining.

events.text: Three of those sworn to {crt_name} have had the same dream this winter, and each thinks it is only theirs. In it the seat is empty and the hall is full of water, and they are bowing to it anyway. They will not speak of this. They will only be, each of them, slightly slower to rise when {crt_he} comes in.

choices.text: Have the dream told to the fourth

effects.log: A word in a wine shop. By spring, all four have had it, or think they have. It comes to the same.

choices.text: Let the water rise by itself

effects.log: You do nothing. There is a good deal of patience in the dead, and you have started borrowing it.

events.text: A young challenger came a long way to meet {crt_name}, {crt_title}, and went home saying it was all true, every word. But the young one's second, who watches feet, told a friend something else: that in the last exchange {crt_name} looked over {crt_his} shoulder. At nothing. In the middle of a duel. It is only a small story. It travels well.

choices.text: Buy the second a drink

effects.log: You buy the drink, and you hear it in full. Then you hear it from two others on the road home, and it has grown.

choices.text: Stay out of it

effects.log: You stay out of it. Stories want no help from you.

events.text: It has got into {crt_name}'s sleep now. {crt_He} has lost a rung of {crt_his} strength and most of {crt_his} nights. {crt_His} {crt_rel}, {crt_kin}, has taken to sitting up with {crt_him}, and has begun to keep a small careful record of what happens at which hour. You would have done the same, once. It is what you would have told someone to do.

choices.text: Pour death qi after it

effects.log: The record gets longer, and the hours worse. You make a point of not reading it.

choices.text: Hold it steady

effects.log: You hold it steady. You have become someone who knows what steady is, in this.

events.text: Water has begun to stand in odd places around {crt_name}: a cup filled overnight, a wet mark on a dry floor, a sleeve that will not dry. A rung of {crt_his} cultivation has run out with it. {crt_kin}, {crt_his} {crt_rel}, mops without a word, and has quietly had the household's letters read aloud, since {crt_his} eyes are going too.

choices.text: Send more of the river

effects.log: It comes up through the floor that week. {crt_kin} moves {crt_him} upstairs and goes on mopping.

choices.text: Let it seep at its own pace

effects.log: You let it seep. It is doing very well without you, and you are not sure how you feel about that.

events.text: You met {crt_name} on the road, by plain chance, the first time in years. {crt_He} has lost a rung and {crt_he} knows it, and {crt_he} still drew {crt_him}self up and gave you the old insult, in nearly the old voice. {crt_kin}, {crt_his} {crt_rel}, took {crt_his} arm and apologised to you. It is an odd thing to be apologised to for that.

choices.text: Give back the old insult

effects.log: You give it back, word for word, as you always did. For a moment {crt_he} looks almost happy. You walk on quickly.

choices.text: Bow, and let {crt_him} have the road

effects.log: You bow and step aside. {crt_He} knows that you have never done that before. It frightens {crt_him} more than anything yet.

events.text: The sect's ledgers have started to go wrong in the hands of {crt_name}, and a rung of {crt_his} strength has gone with them. Sums {crt_he} has done for eighty years. {crt_His} {crt_rel}, {crt_kin}, checks them at night and corrects them in {crt_his} hand, so that nobody will see. {crt_kHe} has become rather good at the handwriting. You have this from the bursar.

choices.text: Send the wonhon into the ledgers

effects.log: A whole province of rents comes out wrong in the spring. {crt_kin} cannot correct that much. It is noticed.

choices.text: Leave {crt_kin} {crt_khis} small mercy

effects.log: You leave it. It is not kindness. You just find that you would rather not be the one to take that away.

events.text: {crt_name}, {crt_title}, has lost a rung, and in a seat like that, it cannot be hidden long. {crt_He} no longer walks the walls. Petitioners are seen by {crt_kin}, {crt_his} {crt_rel}, who speaks for {crt_him} and is watched like a pot. The cousins are very concerned. They have sent gifts of ginseng, and have asked how long it has been going on.

choices.text: Press it while the cousins are watching

effects.log: You press. {crt_name} falls asleep in full audience in front of all of them. Nobody wakes {crt_him}.

choices.text: Let the cousins do the work

effects.log: You let them. There is nothing a curse can do to a great house that the house will not do faster to itself.

events.text: The whole hall stood up for {crt_name} at the spring gathering, as it always does, and {crt_he} could not get out of {crt_his} chair. It took a moment. Only a moment, and {crt_his} {crt_rel}, {crt_kin}, was there at {crt_his} elbow to make it look like a pause. A rung is gone. There were three hundred people in that hall, and every one of them saw the pause.

choices.text: Go to the next gathering yourself

effects.log: You go. You are quite far back. {crt_name} looks over the hall, and for a moment {crt_his} eye rests where you are. It moves on.

choices.text: Pour death qi after it

effects.log: By the next gathering {crt_he} does not stand at all. They say {crt_he} has grown too dignified for it.

events.text: A rung is lost, and the world can count: {crt_name} has dropped places on the Heavenly Rankings, {crt_title} or not. {crt_kin}, {crt_his} {crt_rel}, has started fighting {crt_his} challengers for {crt_him}, so that nobody has to see. {crt_kHe} is doing surprisingly well at it, and {crt_khe} comes home every evening with less of {crt_khim} than {crt_khe} left with.

choices.text: Go and watch {crt_kin} fight

effects.log: You watch one. {crt_kHe} is good, and tired, and has nothing left but this. You make a note. You wish you had not.

choices.text: Send it after the wins, too

effects.log: The next challenger is a boy of nineteen, and {crt_kin} loses to him on a dry floor, slipping on water.

events.text: Abbot Cheonggong has sent a monk down to you, by name, with a basket of pears. He does not know, he says, whose work this is, and he is asking every mudang in the province to pray with them for {crt_name}. The monk is about sixteen. He looks at your rope and blushes for having noticed. Far off, you feel the chanting start again.

choices.text: Pour death qi after it, and pull

effects.log: You wrap the rope around your arm and you pull. Whatever comes of it, it will come of that.

choices.text: Hold still, and let it hold or not

effects.log: You hold still, and you listen to the rope. Nobody ever told you that this would be the hard part.

choices.text: Call it back while you still can

effects.log: You take hold of the rope, and you begin to call. You had not thought you would.

events.text: Seven nights of Mudang Seori's gut at the house of {crt_name}, with the five-coloured cloth down the whole length of the yard. She has had it slit from end to end, the way one opens a road for the dead. You did not know you could feel that from here. She is calling the wonhon of {crt_who} home, by every name it had. She has found out what its mother called it.

effects.log: You take hold of the rope, and you begin to call. You had not thought you would.

events.text: A junior of Wudang has been walking the roads around {crt_name}'s house for a month, with a compass and a bag of nails. Every nail goes into a crossroads. Yun Haksan taught that boy, you can tell from how neatly he walks. There are not many roads left that lead from you to that door. You can feel the rope getting shorter.

events.text: {crt_name} has started to train again. That is all. {crt_He} has lost what {crt_he} has lost, and every morning before light {crt_he} goes out in the yard with the first form anyone ever teaches, and does it badly, and does it again. No wonhon has much to say to that. It is the one thing you were not told how to answer.

events.text: Word comes up the road that {crt_name} has paid a great deal for a mirror of old bronze, and hung it facing the door. It may be a fraud. They mostly are. But your rope has been restless since the day it was hung, and this morning the wonhon of {crt_who}, far off, seems to have seen something in there that it had quite forgotten about.

events.text: The people of {crt_name} have tracked it this far: a physician who reads the pulse of the dead, and a blind woman who follows the cold. {crt_name} is carried from one to the other, and they have started to agree. Nobody has your name yet. But they have marked the road the thing comes by, and they have begun to sit up beside it with lamps.

events.text: It holds. You hear it in the way the rope lies across your knee, heavy and pleased. There will have been a last attempt, a last fee paid, and a kind person explaining to {crt_name} that some things simply run their course. You have a good breakfast. You notice, halfway through, that you have stopped being surprised by this.

choices.text: Finish your breakfast

effects.log: You finish it. The eggs are good. It is all right, as things go, which is the trouble.

choices.text: Go for a long walk

effects.log: You go for a long walk with nobody in it. It does not help, and you are glad to have gone.

events.text: They tried, and it held, and you know a thing now that you did not: how close it was. For a moment on the third night the wonhon of {crt_who} stopped and looked around, as if someone had said its name. You felt it from here. Then it remembered who has it on a rope. It went back to work. You have not slept since, not properly.

choices.text: Tighten the knot a little

effects.log: You tighten it. It does not complain. They do not, and that is the thing about them.

choices.text: Say its name, yourself, once

effects.log: You say what it was called. It does not look around for you. You had not really thought it would.

events.text: {crt_kin} does not know it is you. {crt_kHe} has come to ask you, as a mudang of good name, to perform a gut for {crt_name}, who is failing, and {crt_khe} has saved up to pay your fee. {crt_kHe} would like you to ask the spirits who is doing this. {crt_kHe} says it with such simple trust that the rope goes quiet to listen.

choices.text: Perform it, and call the curse back under cover of the rite

effects.log: You perform it beautifully. {crt_name} sits up on the third day. They tell the whole district about you.

choices.text: Take the fee, and call it back

effects.log: You take the fee. They thank you for it. You will be hearing that thanks for some time.

choices.text: Perform it, and tell {crt_khim} the spirits are silent

effects.log: You go through every step. {crt_kin} bows and pays, and goes home to wait. It is the best gut of your life.

events.text: A letter comes to you, from {crt_name}, in person, written by {crt_kin} since {crt_he} can no longer hold a brush. It does not beg. It says {crt_he} has worked out who it must be, and how long {crt_he} has got, and that {crt_he} would like {crt_his} {crt_rel} to be left out of whatever comes next. It closes very correctly. Below that, {crt_kin} has added one line of {crt_khis} own: Please.

choices.text: Call it back, and send no answer

effects.log: You call it back. You put the letter in the fire. Then you take it out again, a little burned.

choices.text: Name a price for it

effects.log: You write one line back, and it is a number. It is what they would understand of you.

choices.text: Burn it, and go on

effects.log: You burn it. The line at the bottom goes last, for some reason.

events.text: It is nearly done. You can tell from how little the rope is pulling now, like a line with something tired on the end. {crt_name}, {crt_title}, has perhaps a season left, if you do nothing. The wonhon of {crt_who} has come as far back along the rope as it can, and it is looking at you. They do not have much in the way of faces. It has enough.

choices.text: Let it finish

effects.log: You open your hand on the rope. There is no noise at all.

choices.text: Stop here, and leave {crt_him} alive with what is left

effects.log: You stop here. It is not mercy, and nobody will mistake it for that. It may be something worse.

choices.text: Offer it: swear the oath, and live

effects.log: You send {crt_him} the words, by way of the wonhon. {crt_name} has been waiting a long time for someone to offer {crt_him} anything.

choices.text: Call it back, even now

effects.log: You call it back. It comes slowly, and it resents you, and you can feel exactly what it has been eating.

events.text: You go and see {crt_name} at last, in the end; somebody should. You go as a mudang with a bell, among the others who have been sent for. {crt_He} is very small in the bed. {crt_He} looks at you and thanks you for coming, and {crt_he} does not know you, or {crt_he} knows you very well. You will never be sure which. Your hand is on the rope, in your sleeve.

The cousins are sharpening things. Nobody has seen {crt_kin} sleep. One more season and the seat itself will go, and everyone knows it, and the wonhon of {crt_who} sits on the arm of it, waiting for your word.

They only bring {crt_him} the papers later each week, and fewer of them, and {crt_he} seals what {crt_he} is given with a hand that {crt_kin} has to steady. Today {crt_he} asked who the steward was, and it was the same steward as for forty years. The rope lies very quiet. It is your move.

They have a long way to fall, those stairs. The wonhon is standing just behind {crt_him}. It looks to you.

events.text: The news gets to you late, with a bill. {crt_name} left instructions that any mudang {crt_he} had consulted should be paid in full. {crt_He} consulted a good many, near the end. Yours is the smallest sum on the list, for a little advice you once gave {crt_his} people at a distance. You sit with it. The rope is one lighter, and you have been paid.

choices.text: Give the money to the shrine

effects.log: You leave it on the step with no name. Spirit-Mother Bongnye will know. She will use it for rice.

choices.text: Keep it. It is yours

effects.log: You keep it. It buys a very decent cloak. It is warm.

events.text: They say that at the end {crt_name} got up, quite clear in the head, walked to the door and opened it, and said, "Well, come in, then, you have been standing there long enough." Then {crt_he} went back and lay down. {crt_kin} told that story to anyone who would listen. You have now heard it four times, and you would give a good deal to know who {crt_he} was speaking to.

choices.text: Ask the rope

effects.log: You ask. It has nothing to say about that. It has never been so quiet.

choices.text: Tell the story yourself, at the next wake

effects.log: You tell it well. It gets a silence. You find you can do that now, and you are not sure when you learned.

events.text: The great hall is hung in white for {crt_name}, {crt_title}, and it is the largest funeral of the decade. Every house has sent someone. The cousins weep in strict order of seniority. By evening, the talk has moved on to who will sit where, and nobody at all is asking what {crt_he} died of. You had worried about that part. You need not have.

choices.text: Stay for the seating

effects.log: You stay. It is very instructive, and the food is good. You leave before the first quarrel.

choices.text: Pay your respects, and go

effects.log: You bow at the proper place, one more face among thousands. It is, you think, the most anyone will ever know of it.

events.text: You stop it there. It is an odd sort of quiet. {crt_name} is alive, and much reduced, and sleeps with a lamp on. The wonhon of {crt_who} has gone off with what it wanted. What it wanted, you notice, was never any of what you told it. People will say that {crt_he} had a long illness and made a good recovery. Nobody will ever say anything else.

choices.text: Close the matter in your book

effects.log: You rule a line under it. It is a very straight line. You have a good hand for this now.

choices.text: Ask what you are going to do now

effects.log: You ask yourself that over supper. You have been hating {crt_name} for a long time, and the evening is quite long without it.

events.text: You stop it there, and the wet marks dry up from the floors of that house. {crt_kin} tells you all this, as it happens; {crt_khe} has come to thank the whole district's mudang, one by one, for their prayers. {crt_name} will never hold a sword again, but {crt_he} has started asking for {crt_his} soup. {crt_kin} looks ten years older. {crt_kHe} bows to you, and you bow back.

choices.text: Accept the thanks

effects.log: You accept it, in the usual words. It goes down like cold water, and stays there.

choices.text: Say it was none of your doing

effects.log: You say so. It is the nearest to the truth you have told in years. {crt_kHe} thinks you are being modest.

events.text: You stop it there. {crt_name} sold the old house this year, and you saw it go. You also saw the rest of it: the rungs lost, the friends gone, and now {crt_his} sword in a pawnbroker's window with the tassel still on. You could buy it for very little. You have wanted something of {crt_his} for about as long as you have known {crt_him}.

choices.text: Buy the sword

effects.log: You buy it. You hang it on the wall, and it looks like a sword on a wall. You had thought it would look like more.

choices.text: Walk past the window

effects.log: You walk past. You walk past again on the way home. On the third day somebody else has bought it.

events.text: You stop it there. The sect has been very kind. {crt_name} has a sunny room, a junior to fetch and carry, and a title that means nothing. Young disciples are brought to bow to {crt_him} on feast days, and {crt_he} blesses them, and {crt_he} calls them by the names of people who died a long time ago. They are told this is a great honour. Perhaps it is.

choices.text: Go on a feast day, and bow with them

effects.log: You bow with the others. {crt_He} calls you by the name of someone long dead, and blesses you. You had not expected that to be so hard to carry home.

choices.text: Send nothing, and stay away

effects.log: You stay away. There is plenty to do. There are always more of the dead than you can reach.

events.text: You stop it there. {crt_name} has handed up {crt_his} seal, in a very fine ceremony, and been given a garden. The new holder of the seat came out to see {crt_him}, once. {crt_kin}, {crt_his} {crt_rel}, was passed over and has gone away, no one is sure where. The hall has a new banner now. It is a good banner. Everyone agrees that the old one was getting worn.

choices.text: Find out where {crt_kin} went

effects.log: You pay to find out. Nobody knows, and they were paid well to say so. You do not like that.

choices.text: Go and see the garden

effects.log: You go, as a mudang, to bless the plum trees. {crt_He} shows you round, very pleased with the plums. You bless them.

events.text: You stop it there. It is the great houses that surprise you: within two seasons, nobody at the gate has heard of {crt_name} in any way that matters. {crt_He} lives in the back courtyard, and {crt_he} is kept warm. {crt_He} sends down orders still, and they are received with every courtesy. A clerk files them. You have seen the file. It is a thick one, and very neat.

choices.text: Read a page of it

effects.log: You read a page. It is a sensible order about a bridge. Somebody should have done it. You put it back.

choices.text: Leave them their back courtyard

effects.log: You leave them to it. It is more than you would have left yourself, ten years ago. It is less than you thought you would feel.

events.text: You stop it there. {crt_name} took {crt_his} own name off the lists, in the end, by letter, in a good clear hand, before they could do it for {crt_him}. It was widely admired. There is a verse about the letter now. {crt_He} keeps bees in a village that does not read much. You hear that the bees are thriving. You hear rather a lot about those bees.

choices.text: Buy a jar of the honey

effects.log: You send for a jar, through three hands. It is very good honey. You have it on your rice for a month.

choices.text: Stop asking after {crt_him}

effects.log: You stop asking. People go on telling you. It seems you are known as someone who likes to hear about bees.

events.text: It is the first thing you have done in years that nobody asked you to. You sit up on the shrine hill with the rope in your lap and call, and it takes three days. The wonhon of {crt_who} comes back along the road the way a very old dog does. When it is home, you look at each other. {crt_name} will never know. You had not thought about how much you would mind that.

choices.text: Feed it

effects.log: You pour out rice wine for it, in the proper way. It does not need that. You do.

choices.text: Go down and see who is about

effects.log: You go down to the village. A woman asks you to look at her cow. You look at her cow. It is the best day you have had in a long while.

events.text: You call it back and there is no great moment. {crt_name} gets better in the ordinary way, with setbacks. {crt_kin} goes on being suspicious of the broth. Elder Dang Moryeon sends a note that says only: Noted. And the Wudang man, whoever he is this year, walks on past your door without stopping, and you stand there behind it with your heart going like a young thief's.

choices.text: Keep the note

effects.log: You keep the note. It is the shortest threat you have ever been sent, and very well written.

choices.text: Burn the note, and sweep the step

effects.log: You burn it, and you sweep the step, and then you do the neighbour's too, since you are out there.

events.text: You had it all planned, every year of it, and now a fever has got there first, or a fall, or some younger enemy, and {crt_name} is past all your plans. The wonhon of {crt_who} sits on the rope again, a bit damp, and it has no more to say about it than you do. Somebody else has had your revenge. You find you would like a word with them. That is how far this has gone.

choices.text: Go to the funeral, and look at who else came

effects.log: You look over the mourners. There are a good many cold faces, and you might know several of them. You nod to one. They nod back.

choices.text: Let it go

effects.log: You let it go, as far as a person can. It takes the rest of the year.

events.text: You are in the middle of a gut for somebody else's grandmother when it comes home. The bell falls out of your hand. For some minutes the voice coming out of you tells the whole yard about {crt_who}, in detail, and about who it was sent after. The family is too frightened to follow it. Spirit-Mother Bongnye's other students have gone very quiet, and one of them is running up the hill.

choices.text: Let them carry you up to her

effects.log: They carry you. She looks at the state of you, and asks no questions, and sends for her bells.

choices.text: Finish the gut, somehow

effects.log: You finish it. On your feet, mostly by your own name. The grandmother goes home. You do not remember the end of it.

events.text: They broke it in the small hours, and at the same moment every door in your house opened and every lamp went out. The {crt_grade} wonhon is home, and it is not the same as when you sent it. It has been a long way, and been called by name, and refused. It stands in you the way a flood stands in a house. It wants to know what any of this was for.

choices.text: Get to Spirit-Mother Bongnye, however you can

effects.log: You get there on your hands, more or less. There is a look on her face that you have not seen before. She reaches for the bells.

choices.text: Try to answer it

effects.log: You try. You lie on the floor and you try to tell it what this was for. Neither of you is convinced. In the morning it is quieter.

events.text: You are buying thread at a stall when somebody sets a bowl down beside you, and it is {crt_kin}. {crt_kHe} has become exactly what you would have been. {crt_kHe} tells you, quite calmly, about the years since {crt_name}: what {crt_khe} sold, what {crt_khe} learned, and from whom. Some of it is from the Court. "There is a field behind this market," {crt_khe} says. "I paid for the day."

choices.text: Go out to the field

ok.log: You come back alone, and pay for your thread. {crt_kHe} will be a long time getting up from that field, and {crt_khe} will get up.

fail.log: {crt_kHe} paid for the day, and it is worth what {crt_khe} paid. They find you at dusk. Everyone at the market has heard why by then.

choices.text: Say what you did, and ask what {crt_khe} wants

effects.log: You say it across the bowl. {crt_kHe} eats a little. "I wanted you to know I could," {crt_khe} says. {crt_kHe} leaves the field paid for, and empty.

events.text: {crt_name} had a plan. It was rather a good one, by all you can tell; {crt_he} got as far as sealing the letter. They found {crt_him} at the desk with the wax still soft, unable to open {crt_his} hand. It took two people to get the letter out of {crt_his} fingers. They brought it to you, as {crt_he} would know that they would. It has your name on it.

choices.text: Read it, and let the knot rest

effects.log: You read it. It is very well reasoned. You send it back with one error corrected, and {crt_he} does not try anything for years.

choices.text: Burn it unread, and untie the knot

effects.log: You burn it, and then you sit down with the cord. You are so tired of reading other people's letters.

choices.text: Draw it closed

effects.log: You draw it closed, there in the study, with the letter still in your other hand.

events.text: It is the third time now that {crt_name} has gone at that rung. {crt_He} has been told by everyone to stop. {crt_He} has been carried out of {crt_his} seclusion, twice, and now they have put {crt_him} to bed. {crt_He} is lying there with {crt_his} eyes open, doing the breathing forms, very quietly. You can feel it from here, as you might feel a child picking at a knot behind your back.

choices.text: Give the cord a small tug, to tell {crt_him}

effects.log: A small one. The breathing stops, and it does not start up again, not for a season.

choices.text: Untie it. That is enough

effects.log: You untie it. You have come to respect few things in this life. It has been a surprise to you, what they turn out to be.

choices.text: Draw it closed

effects.log: You draw it closed. Nobody will pick at anything again.

events.text: {crt_name} passed you on the road at the Double Ninth, among the crowds. Neither of you stopped. {crt_He} stepped aside for you, with a very small bow, the kind nobody else would see. There is no hate in it these days, or none that shows. A long while under a knot wears a person smooth, and you are not sure if you did that, or the years.

choices.text: Bow back, just as small

effects.log: You bow back. There is nobody else in the world that you have this kind of understanding with. That is not a good thought to have.

choices.text: Look at {crt_his} wrist as {crt_he} goes

effects.log: You look. There is nothing there. There has never been anything there to see.

events.text: You were humming at the well this morning, and the woman next to you asked you what the tune was. You did not know. Then you did. It is a song from the coast, for hauling nets, and you have never been to the coast. Somebody on your rope has been singing it to pass the time on a long job. You stop humming. It goes on a little longer without you.

choices.text: Learn the rest of it

effects.log: You let it teach you. It has eleven verses, and they get worse.

choices.text: Sing something else, loudly

effects.log: You sing a very rude song about a magistrate. The woman at the well joins in. For an hour you are quite all right.

events.text: You have started setting out your things in a different order. The bowl where the cup goes. Your sandals pointing in at the door. It took you a month to notice, and then you remembered where you had seen it: the way they lay things out for someone who is expected back. You put it all right again. You will have to keep doing that, you expect.

choices.text: Put it all back

effects.log: You put it back, every morning, like making a bed. It is one more chore.

choices.text: Leave the sandals as they are

effects.log: You leave them. After all, you are expected back. Everyone is.

events.text: It came to you in the bath-house, plain as anything: {crt_name} has just dropped a cup. You could not say how you know. {crt_He} is three provinces off. You saw the way the tea went over the table, and what {crt_he} said, and the look on the servant. You wash your hair. There is a good deal about that person that you know now, and you did not ask to.

choices.text: Listen for what comes next

effects.log: You listen a while longer, in water going cold. {crt_He} says sorry to the servant. It had not occurred to you that {crt_he} would.

choices.text: Get out and get dressed

effects.log: You get out, you get dressed, and you go and talk loudly to somebody about turnips.

events.text: It is a letter first. {crt_kin} writes to every mudang of the province, the same careful letter, asking only for what is known of curses on the memory. {crt_kHe} has signed it with {crt_khis} own name and, under that, with a small drawing of a face, because {crt_name} cannot read the name any more but likes to see the drawing go out. Yours comes with a reply paper, already paid for.

choices.text: Write back with the cure

effects.log: You write it plainly, on the paper {crt_khe} sent. You do not sign it. {crt_kHe} will wonder, and go on wondering.

choices.text: Write back with a price

effects.log: You write down a sum and a place to leave it. It is only business. It always was.

choices.text: Write that you know nothing

effects.log: You write it, in your best hand. You keep the drawing of the face. You could not tell anyone why.

events.text: {crt_kin} has been to see Mo Sangwol. You would not have thought anyone could do that and walk home; {crt_khe} did, more or less, and a good many things are gone from {crt_khis} face. {crt_kHe} comes to you straight from there. "He says you were his best," {crt_khe} tells you. "He asked me to give you his regards. He does not remember what I am called."

choices.text: Give {crt_khim} the cure. Now

effects.log: You write it out with your hand not quite steady. {crt_kHe} takes it. You ask what else was lost, and {crt_khe} just looks at you.

choices.text: Sell it, as you would to anyone

effects.log: You name a price. It is less than last time, you notice, and you do not know what that means.

choices.text: Send {crt_khim} away

effects.log: You send {crt_khim} away. {crt_kHe} goes, in no hurry. You check the door twice that night.

events.text: The whole house of {crt_name} has come with {crt_kin}, those that are left, standing in a line on the road below the shrine, each with a label sewn on. They have not brought weapons, apart from {crt_khim}. They only stand there. {crt_name} is at the end of the line, smiling at them all, not knowing what the line is for. {crt_kin} steps out in front of the others.

choices.text: Go down, and fight {crt_khim} in front of them

ok.log: {crt_kHe} falls. The line does not move. After a time, they come forward and carry {crt_khim} off, and {crt_name} goes with them, asking who that was.

fail.log: {crt_kHe} has you down in the road, with {crt_khis} hand on the rope, and {crt_khe} says the words. The whole line says them with {crt_khim}. You feel it turn, and start for home.

choices.text: Walk down the line, and say each name to them

effects.log: You know them all. You paid for them. You say each name to its owner, and at the end, the one that matters. Nobody thanks you.

choices.text: Stand at the top, and name your price

effects.log: You name it from up there, so that they will all hear. They pay. It takes every one of them.

events.text: The names go back in a strange order. {crt_name} gets the dog's first, and a cook who left thirty years ago. For a week {crt_he} goes about the house saying them, delighted. {crt_kin} waits. {crt_kHe} has waited this long. Then, one wet afternoon, without looking up from the bowl {crt_he} is eating from, {crt_he} says, "You should get some sleep," and {crt_he} calls {crt_khim} by {crt_khis} name.

choices.text: Hear about it, and say nothing

effects.log: You hear about it third hand. It is told as a story about soup. You go out and split wood for a while.

choices.text: Write the name down in your little book, and cross it out

effects.log: You write it, and you cross it out, and you sit looking at that. It is not a balance. You keep the book anyway.

events.text: They found {crt_name} in a town at the far end of the river, very well liked, sweeping a temple for {crt_his} keep. {crt_kin} came to bring {crt_him} home, with all the papers. {crt_He} looked at them with great interest. {crt_He} thanked {crt_kin} for the trouble, and asked if {crt_khe} had eaten. {crt_kin} stayed for the meal. {crt_kHe} has not gone home, either. It is a nice temple. You could go there and see.

choices.text: Go and see

effects.log: You go in a plain coat, and burn a stick of incense. {crt_He} sweeps around your feet and wishes you a good day. You wish it back.

choices.text: Do not go

effects.log: You do not go. You think about that temple more than you think about most things, and you have never been there.

events.text: You find a bone comb on your pillow, an old one with a name scratched on the spine. That is how Elder Dang Moryeon says he has been in your room. Under the name is the mark of a sect, and a date by which the Court would be pleased to hear of a change in that elder's health. It is a very good comb. It would be a shame to send it back.

choices.text: Keep the comb, and send a wonhon

effects.log: You use the comb for a while. It takes the tangles out. The strongest on your rope sets off at dusk.

choices.text: Send the comb back, snapped

effects.log: You send it back in two pieces. A week later, you find both of them on your pillow, mended.
